agent: OPS - deployment, public infrastructure, 3am failure modes
summary: The stack is genuinely up: helpotron-api (:5000), helpotron-web (:5173) and helpotron-tunnel are all enabled, active and Restart=always, user lingering is on so they survive a reboot, and both the local and the public /api/health paths return 200. The healthcheck is no longer the dead-port-8000 version - it probes :5000, :5173 and the public hostname and it does send Telegram alerts (the wake log proves alerts on 09-11, 09-12 and 09-13). What is broken is everything around the edge. The only backup script, scripts/backup_db.sh:11-17, does not list the production database (data/db/helpotron.db) among its candidate paths, so it would resolve to a 19-day-stale repo-root copy instead, and nothing schedules it at all - the live DB has no backup since 2026-09-01. The API also binds 0.0.0.0:5000 (LAN-reachable), the units set no UMask so the service writes world-readable files that the /uploads proxy then serves publicly with no auth, and the unauthenticated /api/monitors/overview endpoint publicly leaks cost and activity telemetry. Headline fix: repoint and schedule the backup, then bind the API to 127.0.0.1 and set UMask=0077 in the three drop-ins.

findings.title: Production DB has no working backup - the only backup script targets the wrong database and nothing runs it
findings.symptom: If data/db/helpotron.db is lost or corrupted the owner loses every user, credit balance, assignment, study material and feedback row with no recoverable copy. The one script that claims to back it up would print a success line while archiving a different, 19-day-stale file.
findings.root_cause: scripts/backup_db.sh:11-17 lists candidate paths in order: DB_PATH, PROJECT_DIR/helpotron.db, PROJECT_DIR/data/helpotron.db, /var/www/helpotron/helpotron.db, /opt/helpotron/data/helpotron.db. The real DB is data/db/helpotron.db (the default at server/config.py:30 and the value of DATABASE_URL in .env). data/db/ is never in the list, so the loop at scripts/backup_db.sh:20-26 matches PROJECT_DIR/helpotron.db first - a 323,584-byte file at the repo root last written 2026-08-26 15:48. The script also defaults BACKUP_DIR to the VPS-era path /opt/helpotron/backups (scripts/backup_db.sh:7) and no cron entry or systemd timer references it.

findings.title: The API listens on 0.0.0.0:5000 - reachable from every device on the LAN although the tunnel only needs loopback
findings.symptom: Any phone, guest laptop or IoT device on the same WiFi can call the full API directly on http://192.168.86.49:5000 - /api/health, /api/monitors/overview, /api/plans and every authenticated route - without passing through Cloudflare. The WAF, rate limiting and access rules are bypassed entirely.
findings.root_cause: ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-api.service:8 starts uvicorn with --host 0.0.0.0. The tunnel ingress at ~/.cloudflared/helpotron.yml:8 points t2b.helpotron.dpdns.org at http://localhost:5000, so loopback would suffice; 0.0.0.0 is strictly wider than needed. The --forwarded-allow-ips 127.0.0.1 on the same line shows the author expected loopback-only origin access.
evidence: ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-api.service:8 - ExecStart=.../uvicorn server.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5000 --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips 127.0.0.1
measured: ss -ltnp | grep :5000 -> LISTEN 0 2048 0.0.0.0:5000 0.0.0.0:* users:(uvicorn,pid=2392946,fd=15)
measured: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://192.168.86.49:5000/api/health -> 200
contrast, measured: ss -ltnp | grep 5173 -> LISTEN 127.0.0.1:5173 only, so the web tier is correctly loopback-bound
findings.impact: All auth, rate-limit and WAF controls are edge-based, so a LAN peer sees the raw origin. On a laptop carried onto a campus, cafe or hotel network this becomes an internet-facing origin with no edge protection.

findings.title: The public web tier is vite preview, a dev-preview server Vite explicitly disclaims for production
findings.symptom: Every public page load takes an extra hop: browser -> Cloudflare -> cloudflared -> vite preview :5173 -> uvicorn :5000 for /api and /uploads. When either hop stalls the user gets a bare Cloudflare 502 with no way to tell which side broke, and there is no compression or caching policy.
findings.root_cause: ~/.cloudflared/helpotron.yml:5-6 maps the public hostname helpotron.dpdns.org to http://localhost:5173, which is the unit at ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-web.service:8, vite preview --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173. The API is reached only through the preview proxy block at web/vite.config.js:166-183. deploy/README.md and deploy/cloudflared.md still document a tunnel pointing at :8000 and a bare cloudflared tunnel run, so the docs describe a deployment that no longer exists.

Unable to reach the origin service ... dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5173: connect: connection refused / read: connection reset by peer, originService=http://localhost:5173 - the failed hop is the web tier, not uvicorn

measured: systemctl --user show helpotron-tunnel -p NRestarts -> NRestarts=1; journalctl --user -u helpotron-tunnel -> 'Main process exited, code=exited, status=11/n/a' at 2026-09-12 15:04:12 (SIGSEGV, healed by Restart=always)

findings.title: Units set no UMask (0002): the service writes world-readable files, and /uploads is proxied publicly with no auth
findings.symptom: Uploaded user files are created mode 0664 and sandbox directories 0775, so any local account can read them. The same files are served to the whole internet by the web tier: an existing upload returns HTTP 200 with no session, token or signature.
findings.root_cause: None of the three units declare UMask, so they inherit the user manager UMask=0002. systemd-analyze --user security reports the gap directly. web/vite.config.js:175 proxies /uploads to the API and web/vite.config.js:41 deliberately exempts /uploads from the app security headers, so the public proxy path exists because the app exposes that directory.

findings.title: The units receive no environment at all - config arrives only through an import-time load_dotenv, and .env defines JWT_SECRET twice with different values
findings.symptom: Nothing about the API configuration is declared where systemd can see it. 'systemctl --user show -p Environment' is empty and /proc/<uvicorn pid>/environ contains no DATABASE_URL, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY and no JWT_SECRET. Which database and which secret the process uses is decided by Python import order, and .env lines 21 and 46 disagree about JWT_SECRET.
findings.root_cause: helpotron-api.service has no EnvironmentFile= and no Environment= line. server/llm.py:16-21 calls load_dotenv(repo/.env, override=True) at import time and re-pins DATABASE_URL/ENVIRONMENT afterwards. server/config.py:30 reads DATABASE_URL via os.getenv when the config module is first imported. Whichever module is imported first wins; today the config.py default happens to equal the .env value so it works by coincidence. Separately .env declares JWT_SECRET on line 21 and line 46 with two different 64-hex values, and python-dotenv resolves duplicates last-wins, so the line-21 value is dead.
evidence: measured: for u in helpotron-api helpotron-web helpotron-tunnel; do systemctl --user show $u -p Environment; done -> 'Environment=' (empty) for all three; no EnvironmentFiles listed
measured: tr NUL newline < /proc/2392946/environ -> ambient session vars only (HOME, PATH, DISPLAY, XDG_*, ...); no DATABASE_URL, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY, no JWT_SECRET, no SESSION_SECRET

server/llm.py:16-21 - from dotenv import load_dotenv ; _PINNED = {k: os.environ[k] for k in (DATABASE_URL, ENVIRONMENT) if k in os.environ} ; load_dotenv(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / .env, override=True) ; for _k,_v in _PINNED.items(): os.environ[_k] = _v
server/config.py:30 - database_url: str = os.getenv(DATABASE_URL, f'sqlite:///{BASE_DIR}/data/db/helpotron.db')

measured: grep -n '^JWT_SECRET' .env -> 21:JWT_SECRET=<redacted> and 46:JWT_SECRET=<redacted>; sha256-prefix comparison of the two values -> 0a089f9ed95f vs 53db85375e16, i.e. two different secrets under one key

measured: .env key/set audit, values never printed -> 28 keys; OMNIROUTE_API_KEY set (73 chars) and OMNIROUTE_API_BASE=http://localhost:20128/api/v1 set, but ss -ltnp shows nothing listening on 20128 (dead lane, and a violation of the settled OpenRouter-only no-omni-lanes rule). STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and TELEGRAM_* are EMPTY, consistent with /api/health reporting stripe_configured:false.
measured: ps -eo pid,cmd filtered for token/secret/api-key/password/sk- -> no helpotron process carries a secret on its command line (clean)
findings.impact: Production config is invisible to systemd and reproducible only by reading Python import order; any refactor that imports config before llm silently repoints the app at the wrong SQLite file, which per the comment at server/llm.py:12-15 has already happened once. The duplicated JWT_SECRET means a loader change flips the signing secret and invalidates every session at once.

findings.title: The healthcheck detects and alerts, but only on problem-set transition - a persistent problem is alerted once and then silent indefinitely
findings.symptom: The state file currently reads claude-client-down and the last alert of any kind was 2026-09-13T02:40:26Z. The stack has been in a known-bad state for about 28 hours and the healthcheck has said nothing, because silence is its design when the problem set has not changed. If Telegram itself breaks, the only trace is one WARN line in journald that nobody reads.
findings.root_cause: helpotron_healthcheck.sh:73-77 compares the current problem set with the previous one and exits 0 printing 'health OK (unchanged: ...)' whenever they match - it never re-notifies an unresolved problem and has no escalation or digest. There is no prometheus, node_exporter or any scraper unit on this box, and ~/.cloudflared/helpotron.yml sets no logfile or rotation, so logs land in /tmp via the unit StandardError=append.

findings.title: Logs written to /tmp are never rotated and the shipped logrotate rule points at a directory that does not exist
findings.symptom: The units append stdout/stderr to /tmp/helpotron_api.log, /tmp/helpotron_web.log and /tmp/helpotron_tunnel.log with no rotation and no size cap. The logrotate config written for them targets /var/log/helpotron/*.log, and /var/log/helpotron has never existed on this box.
findings.root_cause: The unit files use StandardOutput=append:/tmp/helpotron_*.log. deploy/logrotate.d/helpotron:1 declares the log set as /var/log/helpotron/*.log with 'create 0640 spark spark' (a user that does not exist here), and the file is not installed into /etc/logrotate.d at all. The application's own access logs do rotate correctly (server/access_log.py:66 RotatingFileHandler, 10485760 bytes x 10), so this gap is the systemd stdout stream only.

findings.title: The unauthenticated /api/monitors/overview endpoint is public and leaks cost, token and activity telemetry
findings.symptom: Anyone on the internet can GET https://helpotron.dpdns.org/api/monitors/overview and read live business metrics: total requests, top endpoint names, status-code mix, datalake counts, study and assignment counts, and LLM spend in USD with token totals. It is also the endpoint the healthcheck uses as its liveness probe.
findings.root_cause: The route has no auth dependency and no admin gate, and it is reachable both directly (t2b.helpotron.dpdns.org -> :5000) and through the vite preview proxy (helpotron.dpdns.org/api/... -> :5000). The healthcheck depends on that unauthenticated shape: helpotron_healthcheck.sh:18 and :39 set API=http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/monitors/overview and probe it with curl -fsS.

findings.title: Failure-mode audit: every service auto-restarts and the box survives reboot, so the real gap is detection latency, not recovery
findings.symptom: Nothing in the stack dies silently at the process level. The gap is that an outage beginning and ending between two 30-minute probes is invisible, and a persistent one is alerted exactly once.
findings.root_cause: All three helpotron units are UnitFileState=enabled, WantedBy=default.target, Restart=always, RestartSec=5, and user lingering is on, so they start at boot without a login and heal within about 5 seconds. helpotron-health.timer is enabled and fires OnBootSec=1min then every 30 min. The detection gap is the 30-minute probe interval combined with the transition-only dedup at helpotron_healthcheck.sh:73-77. helpotron-tunnel has After=helpotron-api.service helpotron-web.service but no Requires=, so the tunnel can be up while its origin is not - which is exactly the 2026-09-13 state.

findings.impact: Recovery is handled; detection is not. The 3am answer: if the API died at 3am, systemd restarts it in ~5s and the owner sees nothing at all for a transient death. Only if the API is still down at a :11 or :41 probe does one Telegram alert fire - and then nothing further until it recovers. A crash-looping API is caught within 30 minutes; a 10-minute outage that self-heals is never reported.

fixes.change: Two edits. fixes.change: Add the line UMask=0077 to the [Service] section of all three drop-ins: ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-api.service.d/hardening.conf, ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-web.service.d/hardening.conf and ~/.config/systemd/user/helpotron-tunnel.service.d/hardening.conf. This makes every file the services create owner-only (0600) and every directory 0700, so uploads and sandbox dirs stop being world-readable. Apply with systemctl --user daemon-reload - the units only re-read UMask on the next start, so the change takes effect when the service is next restarted (do NOT restart the owner's services to verify; check the setting with systemctl --user show instead). fixes.risk: UMask=0077 applies to newly created files only. If any external process (the extension, a scraper, a root-owned cron) reads uploads as a group member, that read will start failing. The API and the web tier both run as roni-saguey so their own reads are unaffected. Low risk, high value.

external_research.what: systemd.exec(5) and the systemd --user manager's capability semantics - why a user unit dies with status=218/CAPABILITIES and which sandbox directives are actually available to an unprivileged manager
external_research.why: Explains the exact failure the owner already hit ('Failed to drop capabilities: Operation not permitted', status=218/CAPABILITIES on helpotron-tunnel at 2026-09-11 15:03:27) and validates the existing drop-ins, which correctly omit ProtectKernelModules/ProtectKernelLogs/ProtectClock/PrivateNetwork/ProtectControlGroups. Also identifies the one directive those drop-ins are still missing - UMask - which is the H7-F4 fix.
external_research.verdict: adopt - keep the current safe subset, add UMask=0077, and use 'systemd-analyze --user security <unit>' as the scoreboard (7.9 EXPOSED today). The 218 mechanism is corroborated by the systemd issue tracker: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/33167

external_research.what: Cloudflare Tunnel monitoring - what tunnel 'Healthy' actually measures, and where origin-down 502s become visible
external_research.why: States the single fact this track turns on: tunnel status reflects only the cloudflared-to-Cloudflare connection, so a tunnel can read Healthy while every user gets a 502. That is exactly the shape of this deployment (helpotron.dpdns.org -> :5173 -> :5000) and it means the origin must be probed separately and by the right metric. It also points at cloudflared's own Prometheus metrics - which this box already serves on 127.0.0.1:20241 with 54 series and nothing scraping them (H7-F7).

external_research.verdict: adapt - the instrumentation is already installed and free (cloudflared_tunnel_request_errors and the register-connection metrics on :20241); adopt the layered probe model and skip any new vendor dependency

external_research.what: Vite CLI documentation - the `vite preview` command's intended use
external_research.why: Documents that vite preview is 'intended for previewing the build locally and not meant as a production server'. helpotron's entire public web tier is that command (helpotron-web.service:8, tunnel ingress line 6), so the product's production edge is an unsupported component. Maintainer detail on the missing production features (no gzip/brotli, unoptimised sirv config, no stability guarantee): https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/16607 and https://github.com/vitejs/vite/discussions/2834
external_research.verdict: reject as a production server (recognise the risk); adapt by keeping vite preview only as the local sanity check and serving web/dist behind a real static server or through the existing FastAPI static mount, which also removes the :5173 hop

external_research.what: SQLite online backup API as used by scripts/backup_db.sh
external_research.why: The script's python3 -c 'con.backup(bck)' call is the correct, safe way to copy a live SQLite database without locking writers - so the mechanism is sound and only the path selection and the schedule are broken. This matters because the fix (H7-X1) is a two-line path change plus a timer, not a rewrite. It also justifies backing up to a different filesystem: an online copy on the same disk protects against corruption but not against disk loss.
external_research.verdict: adopt - keep the backup mechanism exactly as written, change CANDIDATE_PATHS to put data/db/helpotron.db first and add the timer plus an off-machine destination
